item.title: Romania Keeps EU’s Highest Rates With Inflation Stuck Above 10%
item.description: Romania held interest rates at the highest level in the European Union as policymakers tackle double digit inflation in an economy on the verge of a recession.

item.title: Former Disney Executive Named CEO of Film Distributor Fathom
item.description: Jason Brenek plans to release more faith-based movies and independent films

item.title: Susquehanna Puts Up $500 Million for ‘Hedging’ World Cup Games
item.description: Susquehanna International Group has lined up $500 million to work with institutions that want to use prediction markets to hedge the economic risks associated with various World Cup outcomes.

item.title: Douglas Elliman Bets on AI to Reinvent Brokerage Business
item.description: Luxury real estate brokerage Douglas Elliman Inc. is betting artificial intelligence can expand its business beyond buying and selling homes.

item.title: AI Firm Zhipu to Sell $4 Billion of Shares After 1,500% Rally
item.description: Chinese artificial-intelligence model maker Zhipu is seeking to raise about $4 billion from a share sale after its stock soared almost 1,500% since a January listing in Hong Kong.

item.title: Pricey Credit Markets Fuel Rise of Funds That Can Buy Anything
item.description: Bond investors are increasingly betting on flexible funds that can buy whatever they like as lofty credit market valuations leave little margin for error.

item.title: Indian Stocks, Rupee Slide After Trump Reignites Iran Tensions
item.description: Indian stocks tumbled and the rupee weakened after oil prices gained following US President Donald Trump’s remark that the tentative ceasefire with Iran had ended after recent attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Coffee Prices to Stay High as Volatility Lingers, Lavazza Says
item.description: The latest bout of volatility in the coffee market is set to linger, complicating the outlook for consumers hoping to see lower prices, according to Italian roaster Luigi Lavazza SpA.

item.title: Argentina to Repay $4 Billion, Defying Critics Who Doubted Tack
item.description: Argentina is set to make a major payment on its dollar bonds this week, pulling off a feat few investors thought possible while the country refuses to tap global debt markets.

item.title: US Heat Sends Power Demand Far Beyond Forecasts
item.description: The country’s biggest grid operator says consumption likely hit a record, smashing a high that had stood for about 20 years.

item.title: State Bank of India Draws Over $1.5 Billion in Offshore Deposits
item.description: State Bank of India has so far raised more than $1.5 billion from foreign-currency deposits under a special program launched last month for overseas citizens, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Samsung Sends Chip Investors on Another Roller Coaster Ride
item.description: The company’s strong earnings fell short of an ever-rising bar for chipmakers

item.title: US Trade Deficit Widens in May to Biggest in More Than a Year
item.description: The US trade deficit widened as imports increased and exports, led by gold, declined.

item.title: Gold Gets a New Shine in Era of Volatile Geopolitics
item.description: Amid the geoeconomic strains of the 2020s, gold’s haven status is proving to be a big beneficiary

item.title: Allianz Unit to Cut as Many as 1,800 Jobs in Push to Adopt AI
item.description: Allianz SE plans to eliminate hundreds of positions at its assistance and travel insurance subsidiary Allianz Partners as the company pushes forward with implementing artificial intelligence solutions.

item.title: Wave of Earnings Surprises Will Be Hard to Repeat, Says Goldman
item.description: The wave of AI-fueled earnings surprises that powered stocks in the last earning season will be tough to repeat, making it unlikely the results alone will spark a major rally, according to Christian Mueller-Glissmann.

item.title: India Seeks Safe Hormuz Passage for Nine Ships as Truce Falters
item.description: India is considering options including holding talks with Iran in order to secure safe passage for at least nine laden tankers waiting in the Persian Gulf, as attacks in the waterway threaten an already fragile interim ceasefire.

item.title: Nvidia Is World’s Most Valuable Company and Cheaper Than Hershey
item.description: Nvidia is relatively cheap despite the continued domination of its chips in AI data centers.

item.title: Dream Finders Homes Boosts Bid for Beazer Homes to $875 Million
item.description: Dream Finders Homes Inc. has boosted its offer for rival homebuilder Beazer Homes USA Inc. to $32 a share.

item.title: SpaceX Bulls Say Full Speed Ahead Despite Wobbles in the AI Trade
item.description: One analyst thinks the company will reach $10 trillion.

item.title: Iluvatar CoreX Seeks to Raise $850 Million After Stock Rally
item.description: Shanghai Iluvatar CoreX Semiconductor Co. is seeking to raise about $850 million from a share sale in Hong Kong after soaring since its initial public offering in January.

item.title: Tesco Explores Sale of Eastern European Business, FT Reports
item.description: Tesco Plc is exploring a sale of its central and eastern European operations, the FT reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Bangladesh Explores Debut Sovereign Bond Sale Overseas
item.description: Bangladesh is studying a plan to issue its first-ever sovereign bond overseas, as the nation looks for ways to finance its record spending.

item.title: India Clears New Derivatives on Index Designed for Foreigners
item.description: India’s market regulator has approved the launch of derivatives on an index designed specifically for foreign investors.

item.title: Hungary Narrows Budget Gap to $10.8 Billion After June Surplus
item.description: Hungary narrowed its first-half shortfall after posting the biggest monthly budget surplus since 2010, helping the new government as it takes on one of the biggest fiscal challenges in the European Union.

item.title: US Stock Futures Slide After Trump Says Iran Ceasefire Is Over
item.description: US equity futures fell as investors turned risk averse after President Donald Trump said the tentative ceasefire with Iran has ended, fueling concerns of a renewal in fighting.

item.title: Apple’s Chip Deal With Broadcom Expected to Exceed $30 Billion
item.description: Apple Inc., following through on a pledge to boost spending on US-made components, said its expanded agreement with Broadcom Inc. is expected to top $30 billion.

item.title: French Watchdog Orders Meta Negotiations Over News Copyright
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. was ordered by the French competition watchdog to hold talks with news organizations over copyright payments, following two complaints that the social media giant was abusing its dominant position.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Extend Loss as Oil Jumps on Iran Risks
item.description: Emerging-market stocks extended losses as an escalation in the Middle East conflict added to the ongoing rotation out of AI beneficiaries.

item.title: Labor Crunch Tests Growth Limits for US Data Center Builders
item.description: Following several quarters of record order books, a skilled-labor shortage is testing the limits of growth for the craft-labor providers who build data centers across the US.
